findings_or_gaps: CRITICAL: pKa1 temperature coefficient is wrong by ~4.3x. Line 79 states pKa1(T) = 6.352 - 0.0238*(T-25). The correct slope from Harned & Davis (1943) is -0.00552/°C, not -0.0238/°C. At the temperature extremes of the stated 15-35°C range, pKa1 errors reach 0.17-0.19 units, far exceeding the document's own ±0.05 pH accuracy target (line 140). This means an implementer following the design note verbatim would produce a solver that gives wrong pH values at any temperature other than 25°C — directly violating the acceptance criterion that implementation can proceed without re-litigating fundamentals.

MINOR: The pH 7.0 fallback for near-zero alkalinity (line 110) is physically incorrect for water containing CO2 (should be acidic, ~pH 5.6 in atmospheric equilibrium), though the note transparently acknowledges this is a stability guard, not a physical model. Acceptable for first pass.

MINOR: The pKa2 fixed value of 10.33 (line 80) is correct at 25°C. The note says the solver interface should keep both constants explicit for later temperature correction — good forward-compatibility design.
follow_up_or_amendments: Replace the linear pKa1 approximation on line 79 with either: (a) the correct linear slope: pKa1(T) ≈ 6.352 - 0.0055*(T-25), or preferably (b) the full Harned & Davis formula: pK1 = 3404.71/(T_C + 273.15) + 0.032786*(T_C + 273.15) - 14.8435, which is only three arithmetic operations and avoids all linearization error across the target range.
If the linear form is kept, add a note that the linear approximation is itself good to about ±0.03 pK units across 15-35°C, and the full formula should be preferred if the temperature range expands.
